notes.text:
This is the ledger of specialized external analytic premises used below. It verifies their exact applicability; it does not prove these foundational product and existence theorems from scratch.

Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), 1–40, DOI 10.1007/BF02392348: [original paper on an author's public site](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf). Printed page 4, equation (2.1), supplies the bounded-psh recursive product. Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 there supply decreasing continuity and symmetric multilinear positive closed products. Theorem 2.4, printed pages 7–9, also supplies decreasing continuity with a bounded-psh multiplier; Theorem 2.10, printed page 10, supplies local mass estimates. Their hypotheses are local boundedness and genuine psh representatives. The introduction uses dd^c_BT=2i∂bar∂=4π dd^c_here. Dividing a b-fold product by (4π)^b transports the statements and recursion exactly. Wedges below are ordinary, without factorial division.

Tosatti–Weinkove, The complex Monge–Ampère equation on compact Hermitian manifolds, JAMS 23 (2010), 1187–1195, DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-2010-00673-X: [primary preprint arXiv:0910.1390v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390). Corollary 1, page 1, equation (1.2), supplies smooth φ and a real constant b with β+i∂bar∂φ>0 and (β+i∂bar∂φ)^n=e^(F+b)β^n for compact Hermitian X, n≥2, and smooth real F. It requires no dβ=0. Taking v=2πφ matches the requested perturbation dd^c_here v. The source constant used in n4 is independently determined by n3.

No Gauduchon metric existence theorem, smooth approximation theorem for all dd^c-closed currents, flow theorem, same-metric theorem or Fujiki-class theorem is needed. Standard measure theory, Hölder's inequality, elementary psh regularization and matrix/exterior algebra are used explicitly below.

notes.summary: A reconstructed: Γ0 is a finite intrinsic measure for every positive (n−1,n−1)-current, including singular coefficients. Auxiliary frames, metrics and dominating measures cancel exactly. Absolute continuity is not claimed at this unrestricted stage.
notes.detailedSummary: A local positive matrix-valued measure K=Dμ gives Γ0=(dV/e^n)^(1/n)det(D)^(1/n)μ. Homogeneity removes changes of μ, congruence and the volume Jacobian remove coframe changes, and H^(1/2) congruence removes the auxiliary metric. Rank deficiency gives zero on mutually singular pieces. Smooth T=γ^(n−1) has Γ0=(γ^n/dV)^((n−1)/n)dV. Arbitrary positive currents can have singular nonzero determinant measure; dd^c-closedness enters in n4.
notes.text:
Let T be any positive (n−1,n−1)-current; dd^cT=0 is not assumed. Positive scalar distributions are Radon measures. Testing against positive rank-one (1,1)-forms and polarizing gives a positive Hermitian matrix-valued coefficient measure. Off-diagonal coefficients are dominated by the sum of diagonal measures: two-by-two positivity implies that a set with zero diagonal trace also has zero off-diagonal coefficients. Radon–Nikodym differentiation against a coefficient-dominating positive measure μ therefore gives a positive semidefinite matrix D μ-almost everywhere. Positivity follows first for a countable dense set of vectors and then for all vectors by continuity.

Fix a local complex coframe θ, e=(i/2)Σθ_j∧bar θ_j and vol=e^n. Use the coefficient convention ξ=(i/2)ΣB_{ji}θ_i∧bar θ_j; transposing matrices converts to the equally usual convention with B_{ij}. Normalize the coefficient measure K=Dμ by
ξ∧T=(1/n)tr(BK).
Then σ_e=(tr D/n)μ. Where c=tr D/n>0, P_e=D/c; where c=0, positivity implies D=0. Thus the proposed measure is locally
Γ0(T)=(dV/vol)^(1/n)det(D)^(1/n)μ. (1)
This normalization includes all ordinary-wedge factorials.

For another dominating measure ν, compare both with λ=μ+ν. If t=dμ/dλ, the coefficient density becomes tD. The identity det(tD)^(1/n)=t det(D)^(1/n), including t=0 and rank deficiency, proves invariance. On t=0 all coefficients dominated by μ vanish. This covers dominating measures that are not mutually absolutely continuous and those containing extraneous mass. Mutually singular coefficient measures are handled through common domination, not products of distributions. For example, disjoint diagonal measures give a rank-at-most-one density on each piece and hence zero determinant for n≥2. Every rank-deficient piece contributes zero.

Under an invertible complex coframe change θ'=Lθ,
B'=L^{-*}BL^{-1}, K'=LKL*, vol'=|det L|^2vol.
Hence det D'=|det L|^2det D, exactly cancelling the volume factor in (1). This applies pointwise to smoothly varying frames, unitary changes and holomorphic coordinate Jacobians. No derivatives of the frame enter.

For an auxiliary metric h with positive relative matrix H in the e frame, h^n=det(H)vol and σ_h=c_Hμ, where c_H=tr(HD)/n. The coframe H^(1/2)θ is h-unitary and
P_h=H^(1/2)DH^(1/2)/c_H.
Its trace is n. Substitution in the stated definition cancels det(H)^(1/n) and c_H, giving (1). If c_H=0, then D=0. Thus auxiliary metrics, frames and all coefficient-dominating measures give the same global measure, including for T=0.

Arithmetic–geometric mean gives det(P_h)^(1/n)≤tr(P_h)/n=1. The smooth ratio (dV/h^n)^(1/n) is bounded on compact X, and σ_h has finite mass. Therefore Γ0(T) is a finite positive Radon measure.

For smooth T=γ^(n−1), with h-relative matrix G, ordinary wedge algebra gives
ξ∧γ^(n−1)=(1/n)tr(B cof G)h^n,
where cof G=det(G)G^{-1}. Since det(cof G)=det(G)^(n−1), formula (1) yields
Γ0(γ^(n−1))=(γ^n/dV)^((n−1)/n)dV. (2)
Also Γ0(cT)=cΓ0(T) for c≥0.

This proves A. It does not assert absolute continuity for unrestricted positive currents: choosing K to be a positive definite matrix times a Dirac measure gives a singular nonzero Γ0. Such a current is generally not dd^c-closed. Absolute continuity for the full admissible family under B's hypotheses is proved in n4.

notes.summary: B reconstructed for genuinely nonclosed β: bounded Hermitian MA mass equals V whenever dd^c(β^j)=0 for every 1≤j≤n−1. Signed global E-powers have the requested recursion and overlap independence; both bounded mass extrema equal V.
notes.detailedSummary: Local bounded psh corrections define E^b as the signed expansion of [dd^c(w+ρ)−dd^cρ]^b, without a local potential for β. The BT recursion gives E^b=dd^c(wE^(b−1)) and glues the products. Pairing with β^(n−b) kills all corrections to total MA mass. Local regularization verifies that the construction is the actual positive bounded Hermitian product. Smooth A=β+dd^cw retains every required dd^c-closed power and satisfies ∫β∧A^(n−1)=V.
notes.text:
Assume β>0 is smooth and dd^c(β^j)=0 for each 1≤j≤n−1; put V=∫β^n>0. Let w be a bounded genuine canonical β-psh function. On a small coordinate ball choose smooth strictly psh ρ with H=dd^cρ≥β. A sufficiently large multiple of |z|^2 works. Then v=w+ρ is bounded psh and Q=dd^cv≥0. H is a closed correction dominating β; it is not assumed equal to β.

Define locally, for 0≤b≤n,
E^b=Σ_(k=0)^b binom(b,k)Q^k∧(−H)^(b−k), E^0=1. (3)
The Q^k are bounded Bedford–Taylor products from n1, so (3) is an order-zero signed closed current. For b=1 it is E=dd^cw. Multiplication by bounded canonical w is meaningful on these measure coefficients.

The local recursive product and its mixed version with smooth closed H give
dd^c[v Q^k∧H^l]=Q^(k+1)∧H^l,
dd^c[ρ Q^k∧H^l]=Q^k∧H^(l+1).
Subtracting, using w=v−ρ, and summing the binomial expansion for E^(b−1) gives
E^b=dd^c[w E^(b−1)]. (4)
There are no missing derivative terms: Q^k and H^l are ∂- and bar∂-closed. The recursion also proves overlap independence inductively. E^0 and E are global; agreement of E^(b−1) and canonical w on an overlap forces agreement of E^b. This covers different corrections and coordinates. Thus all E^b are global d-closed order-zero currents. No local closed potential for β is used.

The actual bounded Hermitian product is the local expansion
(β+E)^k=Σ_(b=0)^k binom(k,b)β^(k−b)∧E^b
=Σ_(b=0)^k binom(k,b)(β−H)^(k−b)∧Q^b. (5)
Multiplication by smooth forms is legitimate whether or not those forms are closed. The first expression and (4) make it global and correction-independent; it agrees with ordinary smooth wedges and the local bounded-potential construction.

Positivity is not inferred from the signed summands. On a smaller ball take radial smooth psh regularizations v_j decreasing to v and put w_j=v_j−ρ. Convolving β+dd^cw≥0 gives
β+dd^cw_j≥−δ_j e, δ_j→0,
for a fixed Euclidean positive form e. The smooth error is β−β*χ_j+H*χ_j−H. Therefore β+dd^cw_j+δ_j e is positive. Its k-th powers converge to (5): decreasing BT continuity handles Q_j^b, while terms containing δ_j vanish by the local mass bounds verified in n1. Consequently (5) is positive and identifies the actual bounded Hermitian product. Canonical representatives matter: arbitrary alterations of w on Lebesgue-null sets are not admissible multipliers in (4).

For a+b=n, distributional duality pairs (4) with any smooth, possibly nonclosed β^a:
∫β^a∧E^b=∫w E^(b−1)∧dd^c(β^a). (6)
The sign is positive; ∂bar∂ is formally self-adjoint in this pairing. If b≥1, either a∈{1,…,n−1} and the hypothesis makes the right side zero, or a=0 and dd^c1=0. Integrating (5) with k=n yields
∫(β+dd^cw)^n=∫β^n=V. (7)
Every bounded genuine β-psh w is included and w=0 is admissible. Thus the infimum v_minus(β) and the corresponding supremum of actual bounded-potential MA masses both equal V.

For smooth w with A=β+dd^cw>0, E is smooth closed. Expanding A^j gives
dd^c(A^j)=Σ_b binom(j,b)dd^c(β^(j−b))∧E^b=0
for 1≤j≤n−1, including the constant power β^0. Similarly,
∫β∧A^(n−1)=Σ_(b=0)^(n−1)binom(n−1,b)∫β^(n−b)∧E^b=V,
using (6) for every b≥1. These identities do not imply dA=0: dA=dβ can be nonzero. This proves B.

notes.summary: C reconstructed over ALL currents and arbitrary smooth probability dV: actual G-sets and intrinsic families are invariant under smooth dd^c perturbations, and the exact endpoint is V^(−1/n)||p||_Ln. Absolute continuity and the sharp L^(n/(n−1)) bound are proved.
notes.detailedSummary: Smooth Hermitian existence with F=log(r^n dV/β^n), followed by n3, determines e^b=V/M on the nonclosed background. The powers T_r=A^(n−1)/V are actual dd^c-closed normalized currents. Matrix AM–GM and testing an arbitrary current give ∫rΓ0(T)≤V^(−1/n)||r||_Ln. Smooth-test duality proves absolute continuity and the density bound without approximating T. The explicit T_r densities give equality for smooth r and the supremum for every real or complex p∈Ln by approximation.
notes.text:
Retain exactly n3's differential hypotheses and any smooth positive probability dV. If h=β+dd^cu>0 for smooth global real u, every positive dd^c-closed current satisfies
∫h∧T−∫β∧T=⟨dd^cT,u⟩=0.
Hence the actual normalized sets G_h=G_β coincide, including singular and degenerate currents. This equality itself needs no differential hypothesis on β. By n2, the entire indexed intrinsic determinant-measure families also coincide.

For smooth r>0 let M=∫r^n dV. Apply n1's Hermitian existence theorem with background β and F=log(r^n dV/β^n). All hypotheses hold. Writing v=2πφ matches the specified dd^c and gives A=β+dd^cv>0 with A^n=e^b r^n dV. The smooth case of n3 gives e^bM=V. Thus
A^n=(V r^n/M)dV. (8)
This determines the source normalization on the nonclosed background in every n≥2.

By n3, dd^c(A^(n−1))=0 and ∫β∧A^(n−1)=V. Therefore
T_r=A^(n−1)/V∈G_β=G_h (9)
is an actual positive smooth normalized current. Formula n2 (2) and homogeneity give
k_(T_r)=V^(−1/n)r^(n−1)/M^((n−1)/n)
=V^(−1/n)r^(n−1)/||r||_Ln^(n−1). (10)
Consequently ∫rΓ0(T_r)=V^(−1/n)||r||_Ln.

Fix any T∈G_β, with no regularity assumed. In a β-unitary frame let B_A be A's positive matrix and P its trace-normalized current density. AM–GM for the eigenvalues of B_A^(1/2)PB_A^(1/2) gives
(1/n)tr(B_A P)≥det(B_A)^(1/n)det(P)^(1/n),
also for semidefinite singular P. Hence, as measures,
A∧T≥(A^n/dV)^(1/n)Γ0(T).
The left side has total mass ∫β∧T+⟨dd^cT,v⟩=1. Substitution of (8) proves
∫rΓ0(T)≤V^(−1/n)||r||_Ln (11)
for every smooth r>0.

Absolute continuity is now proved rather than assumed. Write μ=Γ0(T), already finite by n2, and C=V^(−1/n). For smooth real f, apply (11) to sqrt(f^2+δ^2), then let δ↓0, obtaining |∫f dμ|≤∫|f|dμ≤C||f||_Ln. Uniform smooth approximation extends this to continuous f. If K is compact and dV(K)=0, choose continuous 0≤f≤1 equal to 1 on K and supported in an open set U of arbitrarily small dV-volume. Then μ(K)≤C dV(U)^(1/n), so μ(K)=0. Inner regularity extends this to all null Borel sets, proving μ≪dV.

The continuous-test functional extends to L^n with norm ≤C. L^p duality, q=n/(n−1), supplies nonnegative k_T∈L^q with ||k_T||_Lq≤C. Agreement on continuous tests proves μ=k_TdV. In particular ∫k_T^q dV≤V^(−1/(n−1)). No approximation of the current T was used.

For real or complex p∈L^n, Hölder yields sup_T∫|p|Γ0(T)≤C||p||_Ln. Approximate |p| in L^n by smooth strictly positive r_j. Such approximation follows from smooth real approximants f_j and sqrt(f_j^2+δ_j^2). Formula (10) and the uniform density bound give
∫|p|k_(T_rj)dV≥C||r_j||_Ln−C||r_j−|p|||_Ln→C||p||_Ln.
Therefore
sup_(ALL T∈G_h)∫|p|Γ0(T)=V^(−1/n)||p||_Ln. (12)
For p=r>0 smooth, T_r attains equality. For arbitrary p, only the claimed supremum is required. The entire admissible family and arbitrary fixed smooth probability dV have been retained. This proves C.

notes.summary: D reconstructed: the closed torus family has global least eigenvalue ε and uniformly bounded smooth coefficients and potentials, while its actual full determinant families, sharp endpoint and both bounded MA mass extrema stay fixed.
notes.detailedSummary: Ordinary wedges give ∫β^n=n!, and dd^cφ(x1)=φ″β1/(4π), verifying uε exactly. The diagonal eigenvalues are aε,1,…,1 with ε≤aε≤2−ε. The smooth semipositive limit loses one eigenvalue at x1=0,1/2. Each positive member is Kähler, hence balanced and pluriclosed. The torus has trivial canonical and cotangent bundles. Applying n3–n4 gives equality of actual full current/measure sets and both mass extrema.
notes.text:
On X=(C/(Z+iZ))^n, each x_j,y_j has period 1 and
β_j=(i/2)dz_j∧dbar z_j=dx_j∧dy_j, β=Σβ_j.
Thus β is globally positive and closed, β^n=n!Π_jdx_j∧dy_j, V=n!, and dV=β^n/V is the product probability volume. The dz_j trivialize the holomorphic cotangent bundle, and dz_1∧…∧dz_n trivializes the canonical bundle. Therefore ordinary real c1(X)=0.

For φ(x_1), direct differentiation gives
dd^cφ=(φ″/(4π))β_1. (13)
The prescribed u_ε=(1−ε)cos(4πx_1)/(4π) is globally periodic. Equation (13) gives
dd^cu_ε=−(1−ε)cos(4πx_1)β_1,
ω_ε=a_εβ_1+Σ_(j≥2)β_j,
a_ε=1−(1−ε)cos(4πx_1).
For 0<ε≤1, its eigenvalues relative to β are a_ε,1,…,1, with ε≤a_ε≤2−ε≤2. Equality a_ε=ε occurs at x_1=0,1/2. Hence the global least relative eigenvalue is exactly ε and εβ≤ω_ε≤2β. 'Least eigenvalue ε' means the global minimum, not equality at every point.

Each ω_ε is closed because β and dd^cu_ε are closed. It is therefore Kähler, balanced and pluriclosed. Every fixed-order coefficient derivative is bounded independently of ε: the only varying coefficient is a fixed-frequency trigonometric function of bounded amplitude. Similarly ||∂^m u_ε||_∞≤(4π)^(m−1), with m=0 giving 1/(4π). As ε↓0, coefficients and potentials converge in C^∞. The limit is smooth semipositive, of rank n−1 at x_1=0,1/2 and rank n elsewhere.

The background β satisfies n3. Applying n4 to h=ω_ε proves that actual full sets G_(ω_ε)=G_β and entire intrinsic measure families are identical for all ε, with endpoint (n!)^(−1/n)||p||_Ln for every p∈L^n(dV). By n3, dd^c(ω_ε^j)=0 for j≤n−1 and ∫ω_ε^n=V. Applying n3 again with ω_ε as background proves both bounded-potential mass extrema equal V. Alternatively, w↦u_ε+w is a bijection between canonical bounded ω_ε-psh and β-psh potentials, preserving their actual currents and products.

This proves D. It is degeneration among Kähler metrics on an already Kähler manifold, not a non-Kähler example. check_algebra.py independently checks the operator factor and trigonometric identities.

notes.summary: E reconstructed in every n≥2: genuinely nonclosed positive pluriclosed Ωε keep fixed nonzero exterior derivative, exact full determinant data, both positive mass extrema and balanced trace, yet their global least eigenvalue is ε→0.
notes.detailedSummary: The two-factor block q satisfies q^2=2(aε−τ^2s^2)β1β2 and q^3=0. The exact higher-power expansion has only its 0-, 1- and 2-block terms, all dd^c-closed. The lower eigenvalue bound follows from det(q−εI)=[2(1−ε)^2−τ^2]s^2≥0; equality occurs at s=0. Integration gives Vτ=n!(1−τ^2/2) and balanced trace n!. The nonclosed hτ meets n3–n4 for arbitrary fixed smooth probability dV. The manifold remains the same Kähler torus.
notes.text:
Use n5's torus. Fix 0<τ<1/2, s=sin(2πx_1), and
ξ=(i/2)(dz_1∧dbar z_2+dz_2∧dbar z_1)=dx_1∧dy_2+dx_2∧dy_1.
These tensors are globally periodic. Set h_τ=β+τsξ and Ω_ε=h_τ+dd^cu_ε, 0<ε≤1/2. Their first-two-coordinate matrices relative to β are
H_τ=[[1,τs],[τs,1]], Q_ε=[[a_ε,τs],[τs,1]],
with remaining eigenvalues 1. Since 1±τs>0, h_τ>0. The identity cos(4πx_1)=1−2s^2 gives a_ε=ε+2(1−ε)s^2.

The matrix Q_ε−εI has nonnegative diagonals 2(1−ε)s^2 and 1−ε and determinant
[2(1−ε)^2−τ^2]s^2.
For ε≤1/2 its coefficient is at least 1/2−τ^2>0. Hence Ω_ε≥εβ>0. At s=0 its block is diag(ε,1), so the global least eigenvalue is exactly ε. Since tr Q_ε=a_ε+1≤3−ε<3, positivity gives Ω_ε≤3β in every dimension.

Closedness fails explicitly:
dΩ_ε=dh_τ=2πτ cos(2πx_1)dx_1∧dx_2∧dy_1. (14)
Indeed ds∧ξ kills the dx_1∧dy_2 term and gives exactly the displayed remaining term. This is the same nonzero exterior derivative for every ε.

For the higher-dimensional calculation write
q=a_εβ_1+β_2+τsξ, η=Σ_(j≥3)β_j, Ω_ε=q+η.
The form η is closed. First-two-factor wedge algebra gives
β_1∧ξ=β_2∧ξ=0, ξ^2=−2β_1∧β_2,
q^2=2(a_ε−τ^2s^2)β_1∧β_2, q^3=0. (15)
Consequently the actual ordinary wedge expansion is
Ω_ε^j=η^j+jq∧η^(j−1)+binom(j,2)q^2∧η^(j−2), (16)
with the last term omitted when j=1. This also works for n=2, where η=0 and η^0=1.

For a coefficient g(x_1) multiplying a constant form χ,
dd^c(gχ)=(g″/(4π))β_1∧χ.
Thus dd^cq=0: the varying coefficients multiply β_1 or ξ, both annihilated by wedging β_1. Likewise dd^c(q^2)=0 because (15) contains β_1∧β_2. Since η is ∂- and bar∂-closed, (16) proves dd^c(Ω_ε^j)=0 for every j≤n−1. Taking a=1 proves dd^c(h_τ^j)=0 for every such j. This verifies all higher-power hypotheses, not just pluriclosedness in dimension two.

Only the two-block term contributes to the top power. Using η^(n−2)=(n−2)!Π_(j≥3)β_j gives
Ω_ε^n=n!(a_ε−τ^2s^2)Π_jβ_j,
h_τ^n=n!(1−τ^2s^2)Π_jβ_j.
The averages of a_ε and s^2 are 1 and 1/2. Therefore
∫Ω_ε^n=∫h_τ^n=V_τ=n!(1−τ^2/2)>0. (17)
Also
Ω_ε∧β^(n−1)=((a_ε+n−1)/n)β^n,
∫Ω_ε∧β^(n−1)=n!. (18)
Off-diagonal terms have zero trace. The fixed β is closed, hence balanced, and distinct from these nonclosed metrics. The torus has trivial canonical bundle, real c1=0, and is already Kähler.

All fixed-order derivatives of a_ε, τs and u_ε are uniformly bounded in the fixed β frame. They converge in C^∞ to the ε=0 formulas. The limit is semipositive, with block determinant (2−τ^2)s^2 and block diag(0,1) at s=0. It has rank n−1 at x_1=0,1/2 and full rank elsewhere.

The genuinely nonclosed background h_τ satisfies every hypothesis of n3. For any fixed smooth positive probability dV, n4 therefore proves actual full set equality G_(Ω_ε)=G_(h_τ), equality of their entire intrinsic determinant-measure families, and
sup_(ALL T∈G_(Ω_ε))∫|p|Γ0(T)=V_τ^(−1/n)||p||_Ln
for every real or complex p∈L^n(dV). Equations (16)–(17) allow n3 to be applied separately to each Ω_ε: both bounded-potential mass extrema are V_τ. The canonical bounded-potential bijection w↦u_ε+w gives the same conclusion.

This proves E for every n≥2. check_algebra.py additionally verifies these exterior-power, derivative, volume and trace identities by exact symbolic calculations for n=2,…,6. General dimension follows from (15)–(16), not extrapolation from those finite checks.

notes.summary: F reconstructed: bounded canonical torus potentials concentrate in every dimension, attaining the sharp determinant-power norm with varying dual maximizers. Actual currents converge to a normalized BT current with Γ0=0; Γ0 masses vanish while determinant-power integrals fail to be continuous.
notes.detailedSummary: The Poisson series verifies the potential with the specified dd^c factor. The summable 1/m² majorant gives uniform convergence to a continuous bounded canonical potential. Its first-factor curvature is δ_{x1=0}dx1∧dy1, whose bounded BT square is zero. Explicit powers prove current convergence and actual MA mass V. Relative to mutually singular Lebesgue and hypersurface measures, the limiting current matrices have ranks 1 and n−1, so Γ0 vanishes. Actual MA, determinant-power and determinant measures have distinct limiting behavior. No fixed common density, fixed dual maximizer or uniform coefficient bounds are claimed.
notes.text:
Use n5's β, V=n! and product probability dV. For 0<ε<1 set r=1−ε. Summing two geometric series gives
P_r(x)=1+2Σ_(m≥1)r^m cos(2πmx)=(1−r^2)/(1−2r cos(2πx)+r^2).
It is positive, smooth, periodic, and has integral 1. Hence f_ε=ε+(1−ε)P_r>0 and ∫f_εdV=1.

The supplied series
w_ε=−[2(1−ε)/π]Σ_(m≥1)r^m cos(2πmx_1)/m^2
is smooth for fixed ε>0, with termwise differentiable series of every order. Applying (13) gives
dd^cw_ε=2(1−ε)Σr^m cos(2πmx_1)β_1=(f_ε−1)β_1.

This rejects an ellipticity implication from those data alone. A pointwise determinant lower bound plus a pointwise upper metric bound would prevent degeneration; the aggregate determinant endpoint does not provide that estimate. No flow trajectory, long-time existence, convergence, non-Kähler example or priority claim is proved. notes.text:
A–G have been reconstructed within their stated limited scope, using the two checked external analytic premises in n1. This does not complete the unrestricted geometric task.

For G, fix τ and any smooth probability dV and take ε↓0 in n6. The actual full current sets remain G_(h_τ), and every intrinsic measure indexed by those currents remains the same. Thus even the entire determinant-measure family, not just its endpoint, is fixed. The endpoint for each fixed p is V_τ^(−1/n)||p||_Ln. Both bounded-potential mass extrema remain the same positive V_τ. The torus has real c1=0, and Ω_ε's coefficients and u_ε have uniform C^m bounds for each fixed m. The separate balanced β gives constant trace ∫Ω_εβ^(n−1)=n!, and dΩ_ε is fixed and nonzero. Nevertheless the global least eigenvalue is ε. No constant c>0 independent of ε can satisfy Ω_ε≥cβ. This proves the limited obstruction including genuine nonclosed pluriclosed metrics. The closed family n5 supplies the simpler version.

One precise missing estimate can be described by elementary eigenvalue algebra. If relative eigenvalues satisfy λ_j≤Λ pointwise and Π_jλ_j≥δ>0 pointwise, then λ_min≥δ/Λ^(n−1), because Π_jλ_j≤λ_minΛ^(n−1). A pointwise volume-density lower bound combined with a pointwise upper metric bound would therefore prevent this degeneration. In n6 the upper bound Ω_ε≤3β already holds, but its determinant at s=0 is ε. The required determinant lower bound fails. The fixed determinant profile concerns normalized dd^c-closed test currents and cannot supply that missing pointwise estimate. Additional estimates involving particular densities, torsion norms measured in the evolving metric, curvature or initial pointwise data are not excluded. Fixed-background smooth coefficient bounds do not themselves bound torsion in a degenerating metric.

Scalar perturbations preserve d(h+dd^cu)=dh, since ddd^cu=0. The nonzero derivative in n6 verifies this in an actual family. Therefore n4's scalar prescribed-volume construction does not produce closed positive (1,1)-data from a nonclosed metric. These examples are on an already Kähler torus and do not disprove the balanced/pluriclosed coexistence conjecture. The parameter ε is not flow time; no family is offered as a pluriclosed-flow trajectory. No flow evolution, normalization, admissible-data theorem, long-time existence or convergence is established.

Original completion remains open: this work constructs no closed Kähler current from arbitrary coexistence and proves no flow convergence under the original real-c1 hypothesis. The same-metric and Fujiki-class observations are not substitutes for those conclusions. Literature priority and novelty of the two-factor torsion mechanism are not certified. Accordingly candidate=false.
